correctness.rationale: For each tree on \(n\ge3\) vertices, a tree-incidence basis has absolute maximal minors 1, giving Gram determinant n and volume \(2^{n-1}\sqrt n/(n-1)!\) and a lattice-equivalent standard crosspolytope. Exact intrinsic Gaussian radial decomposition gives width \(2\mathbb E M_T/a_{n-1}\). Conditional on the index and magnitude of the sample largest absolute Gaussian, any fixed neighbor is half-normal truncated above the maximum, proving a uniform additive lower loss at most sqrt(2/pi). A 2(n-1)-variable variance-two exponential-moment bound proves the upper; disjoint path edges and hub leaves give sharp Gaussian extremes. A uniform O(log n) second-moment estimate justifies expected broom maxima. Exhaustive 1,440 finite tree Gram determinants and 2,250 sampled support comparisons passed, but those samples are not relied on for universal limits. The α=1 endpoint is handled separately as the pure path.

value.rationale: All n-vertex tree symmetric edge polytopes have identical face vectors, Ehrhart polynomials and Euclidean volumes in the canonical root realization. A sharp full continuum of different leading-order Euclidean mean widths is therefore a naturally motivated geometric classification not encoded by any of those invariants. The uniform endpoint bounds and every-constant broom construction resolve the all-tree asymptotic range rather than recording a routine fixed finite example; no downstream paper-scale conjecture is claimed.
